rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0005, proj_sr=0.0005, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-6 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: projection-domain BF RANGE sigma proj_sr 0.02->0.0005 (edge-preserving), keeping the iter-5 WINNER img_sr=0.0005. BREAKTHROUGH PRIOR: iter-5 (img_sr 0.02->0.0005) hr=0.1257, SSIM0.9605, PSNR39.57, recon_rmse8.61e-4 < baseline9.84e-4 -- the FIRST recon to BEAT the 128-view FBP. Root cause: a TIGHT range sigma makes the image BF EDGE-PRESERVING (smooths flat noise, stops at fibroglandular edges) instead of over-smoothing. Iters 1-4 (wide sr=0.02, depth, n_iter) all floored at hr=0 = confirmed the wide-range BF was the over-smoothing culprit, not the N2I loss per se. HYPOTHESIS: the SAME edge-preserving fix in the PROJECTION domain (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) suppresses sparse-view streak noise in the sinogram before FBP WITHOUT the view-inconsistency that a strong-but-wide proj filter causes (findings.md: keep proj filtering gentle/soft -- a tight RANGE sigma is soft-edged in intensity, exactly the recommended lever) -> hr climbs above 0.1257. If hr drops vs iter-5, proj-domain edge-preservation induces view inconsistency and the image domain alone is the safe lever. BUDGET: value change only, ~1020s like iter-5. ONE knob: proj_sr 0.02->0.0005.
